feedback: This candidate shows a well-reasoned improvement over the previous design by increasing base_speed to 1.5 to target the required average speed for course completion under 3 seconds. The reduction of integral gain ki to 0.2 aims to reduce overshoot and oscillations, which should improve stability. The sensor weights have been adjusted to [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], increasing sensitivity on the outer sensors to enhance steering precision. The geometry remains unchanged, preserving the balanced physical design. However, without telemetry data from a race, we cannot yet confirm if these changes reduce line loss events or steering oscillations as intended. To verify and refine, please try: 1) Slightly increase kd from 2 to 3 to improve damping of oscillations. 2) Adjust sensor_weights to [-1.5, -1, 0, 1, 1.5] to test if slightly lower outer weights reduce oversteering. 3) Keep base_speed at 1.5 to maintain target speed while tuning control gains for stability.
